text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000146 bills 99215 well above expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, but the few documented 99215 charts support the billed level, so the records are too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is concerning: the 99215 share is elevated in every complexity stratum, not just among sicker patients. Most sampled low-complexity 99215s carry only minor or acute diagnoses, such as rash (C0075028, C0075079, C0075088, C0075177), upper respiratory infection (C0075071, C0075332) and abdominal pain (C0075267, C0075289), which rarely warrant high-complexity decision-making. Against that, all three documented 99215s were supported at high MDM, including C0075150, a single-condition patient with 49 minutes recorded. With only three such charts, the documentation is too thin to judge either way. The 37% 'problems' note-signal rate and the one undersupported 99214 (C0074719, which also appears among the problem-flag examples) are worth a look but are not decisive, and no audit trail was received to test for cloned or inflated notes. A reviewer should first request records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the zero-condition acute-diagnosis visits, and the audit trail, to see whether documented MDM or time actually supports level 5."}
